title: Chicken Wing Bar Night
seoTitle: Chicken Wing Bar Night | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crispy baked wings with three sauce options for ten
subtitle: Crispy baked wings with three sauce options for ten
description: Wings are baked on racks until skin crisps, then tossed in separate bowls of buffalo, honey-garlic, and BBQ sauce. Celery, carrots, and ranch complete a classic wing bar that scales to any appetite.

ingredients.name: chicken wings
ingredients.notes: split into flats and drums; about 12 oz raw per firefighter

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Chicken Wing Bar Night in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Dry and season wings
steps.instruction: Pat wings completely dry. Toss with baking powder, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Arrange skin-side up on wire racks with space between each piece.

steps.title: Bake until crisp
steps.instruction: Bake at 425°F for 25 minutes, flip, then bake 20–25 minutes more until skin is golden and thickest drum hits 175°F internal. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Build the three sauces
steps.instruction: Simmer butter with hot sauce for buffalo. Warm BBQ sauce separately. Sauté minced garlic 1 minute, stir in honey and a splash of soy for honey-garlic.

steps.title: Toss and line up the bar
steps.instruction: Divide wings into three bowls and toss each batch in its sauce. Arrange on a long board with labeled sauce ramekins for second passes.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Chicken Wing Bar Night onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Set the wing bar
steps.instruction: Lay out celery, carrot sticks, and ranch dressing. Verify all wings hit 165°F minimum before service—even sauced wings must be safely cooked.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Chicken Wing Bar Night — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Baking powder dries the skin—do not substitute cornstarch; results differ.
Hold unsauced wings at 200°F and toss to order if you need maximum crunch late in the game.
Save wing tips for stock or discard—flats and drums portion cleaner for a hall feed.
tonightSpread: Three-sauce wing bar with celery, carrots, ranch, and blue cheese dressing.
Waffle fries or tater tots from the oven for a full sports-bar spread.
leftovers: Re-crisp sauced wings in a 400°F oven 5 minutes on a rack.
Pull meat for buffalo chicken mac and cheese tomorrow.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Wing bars let everyone pick their heat level without cooking three separate batches from scratch. Baking keeps the kitchen cleaner than deep frying while still delivering crisp skin.
mealPrepNotes: Dry wings overnight uncovered in the fridge for maximum crispness. Sauce can be mixed ahead and held warm. Bake in two batches on double racks if your oven is standard size.
